jobs.title: VP, Consulting & Transformation
jobs.description:
Domaine is a global digital commerce and transformation partner for ambitious and beloved brands. We are the world’s largest independent Shopify partner. We are also a growing team of strategists, designers, engineers and specialists who help brands decide where to invest, build what comes next, and run it at scale across platforms, channels and AI. As pioneers and not just participants in our industry, we are inspired to write, break, and re-write the rules for a new generation of commerce.

The VP, Consulting leads Domaine’s Consulting practice and holds a seat on the Craft Leadership team. The practice brings together multiple disciplines: Strategy, AI and Transformation Advisory, CRM and Lifecycle, Conversion Rate Optimization, and SEO/GEO/AEO. This role owns consulting as a commercial function as well as an advisory one. It is how Domaine moves from being chosen for a platform build to being chosen for the business outcomes.

This role does not receive a brief and execute it. It takes in a conversation with a prospect or existing client, specific or vague, and discerns the goals, the real needs, the gaps, the path, and the teams and skills required to get there. It then builds the plan and the trust to see it funded. It works in lockstep with Client Partners, Creative, Sales and Engineering, and brings commercial instinct to every recommendation: what should change, why it will grow the client’s business, what it will cost, and what it will return.

Responsibilities

Consulting Leadership

Lead senior engagements for clients including digital and AI transformation, platform and replatforming decisions, international expansion, B2B, retail and POS, loyalty, marketplace, data, and operating model.
Run structured Discovery across business objectives, customer insight, data, technology, organization and operating model. Translate it into goals, needs, gaps, a sequenced path, and the capabilities and skills required.
Build the business case that turns a roadmap into funded work and prioritization by business impact, customer impact, level of effort, and dependency.
Produce multi-year roadmaps to show the art of the possible and how they get there.
Recommend what Domaine should and should not do. Where a client’s best path goes beyond our delivery, build the partner or co-delivery model rather than shrinking the recommendation.

Retention, Account Expansion, and Commercial Growth

Own the 1, 3 or 5 year plan for every top-tier retained client, tied to their stated business goals. A launch is the beginning of our relationship with the client, not the end.
Chair or co-chair Growth Councils and QBRs with the Client Partner, run as forward-looking conversations with explicit ROI accountability rather than a retrospective of work delivered.
Support the orchestration of a unified team for every retained client, synthesizing strategy, AI and transformation, CRM and lifecycle, Conversion Rate Optimization, SEO/GEO/AEO, Design, and Technology perspectives into a single narrative. Help evolve accounts from single-threaded delivery to multi-service relationships.
Provide the strategic input and human judgment layer on client health and monthly intelligence reporting, on top of AI-generated analysis.
Ensure consulting hours are named, scoped, and priced into retainers and new builds rather than absorbed into the account.
Join pursuits for strategic accounts, bringing senior transformational thinking into the room alongside Sales and Client Partners.
Help shape scope before pricing on complex or multi-discipline engagements, so the approach differentiates the proposal rather than reading as a deliverable list.
Own the strategic spine of Domaine’s pitch narrative, positioning Domaine as a digital services partner and not only a platform implementer, and keep it current as the market moves.

Practice Leadership and Partner Advisory

Fluent in every discipline they lead. Knows Strategy, CRO, CRM and Lifecycle, SEO/GEO/AEO and our emerging AI services from the inside: the KPIs that run each one and how each should be applied to project and retained work.Own quality, methodology and playbooks, team structure, performance management, and day-to-day operation.
Carry practice margin and utilization targets.
Build the documentation, frameworks, and evaluation criteria that let each discipline scale past the people currently doing the work.
Turn proven pilots, including managed services and Domaine Labs and AI Commerce capabilities, into standard offerings with defined scope and pricing.
Help shape Domaine’s point of view on the digital commerce stack beyond the storefront: search and discovery, personalization, lifecycle and messaging, loyalty, subscription, PIM, ERP, OMS, DAM, data, and the AI tooling layer around them.
Advise clients on whether their current stack supports their goals and competitive needs, and where to reinvest. Consulting evaluates whether the investment holds up against the client’s growth plan.

Practice and People Leadership

Support the enablement of applied AI so it shows up in client roadmaps as measurable, and bring AI-differentiated capability into sales conversations, including AI discoverability, agentic commerce operations, and partner stack advisory.
Redefine consulting and discipline deliverables for an AI-native workflow, with measurable impacts.
A leader the practice leads trust. Mentors the discipline leads, earns their confidence, and pushes each practice toward continual improvement and revenue growth.Set performance standards and build a bench that can operate without you in the room.
Hold the layer below accountable as leaders owning outcomes.

Qualifications

10+ years in consulting, strategy, or senior client leadership, with meaningful time in a client-facing senior role at an agency, digital consultancy, or consulting firm.
Track record of leading digital transformation engagements from an ambiguous problem to a funded roadmap to a delivered outcome.
Experience running a consulting or strategy function and a multi-discipline group: defining the offering, setting methodology, carrying a commercial number, and building and leading leaders.
Demonstrated experience building and defending a business case for a digital transformation initiative, including ROI modeling and prioritization frameworks.
Track record of growing retained or recurring revenue relationships, not only winning net-new business.
Strong command of the digital commerce growth model: demand generation, conversion, lifecycle and retention, merchandising and AOV, and the data that connects them. Enough depth to make credible recommendations and lead discipline leaders.
Fluency in the commerce ecosystem and the surrounding partner, app, and enterprise systems landscape.

Perks & Benefits

Competitive Healthcare with Dental & Vision
Retirement savings plan with employer matching
Competitive PTO policy with paid time off at end of year
Flexible working schedule
Remote-first culture
Home office stipend
Apple gear
Continued education and personal development opportunities

We are an Equal Opportunity employer. We do not discriminate in hiring on the basis of sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religious creed, national origin, physical or mental disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law.

jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the opportunity?

As Director, Financial Crimes Risk Assessment you are responsible for the design and execution of the enterprise risk assessment. In this role, you will identify and assess inherent risks and control effectiveness, demonstrate compliance, and identify opportunities to optimize the financial crimes program, by:

Leading the enterprise-wide assessment of financial crimes risks and controls globally and across RBC Platforms, businesses units, and jurisdictions.
Leading the development of capabilities to enable the quantitative and qualitative assessment of inherent risks, control effectiveness, and residual risk.
Performing expert analysis to identify concentrations of risk and adequacy of controls to ultimately inform and recommend risk mitigation strategies.
Delivering high-quality risk assessment products to support regulatory compliance and inform business decisions.
Remaining abreast of emerging risks and evolving regulatory environment to continuously refine RBC’s risk assessment approach.

What will you do?

Lead the efficient and effective execution of enterprise-wide risk assessment activities, in line with regulatory and business expectations.
Lead the development and continuous improvement of the Enterprise Risk Assessment Methodology and operating procedures.
Identify gaps and opportunities to enhance risk assessment data integration, tools, and processes to drive efficiency and consistency across assessments.
Identify requirements for analytic tools and capabilities to perform quantitative and qualitative assessments of inherent risks, controls and residual risk
Collaborate across financial crimes program to establish risk rating frameworks, validate results, align on mitigation strategies and produce reports.
Establish roadmaps and provide regular reporting on risk assessment activities including data collection and integration, analysis and report generation.
Identify and escalate material risk exposures and control gaps
Support regulatory exams, audits and internal reviews related to risk assessment activities
Monitor changes in AML/ATF regulations and participate in industry related initiatives to remain abreast of existing and new laws and regulatory expectations

What do you need to succeed?

Must have

Post-secondary education or equivalent
Proven experience with executing financial crime risk assessments
Strong ability to evaluate and design risk assessment capabilities and tools
Deep understanding of global financial crime regulatory environment
Ability to synthesize complex data into clear, actionable insights
Experience working with cross-functional teams
Project management

Nice to have

Graduate degree (MBA or relevant subject matter area)
Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist (CAMS) designation or other related certifications

What’s in it for you?

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits, competitive compensation, commissions, and stock where applicable
Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities
Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team
To be part of a large and growing global organization which puts client interests first and has a culture of fairness and accountability

Job Skills

Anti-Money Laundering (AML), Control Analysis, Cross-Functional Leadership, Data Analysis, Data Literacy, Executive Reports, Financial Crimes Compliance, People Management, Professional Writing, Project Management, Regulatory Risk, Risk Assessments, Risk Mitigation Strategies

jobs.title: Director of Operations
jobs.description:
Collections, Customer Experience, General Management, Operations, Property Management, Vendor Management

Compensation

Up to $200,000 CAD annually
, including base salary and performance-based bonuses. Final compensation will be discussed during the interview process and will depend on experience, qualifications, leadership background, and overall fit.

About The Role

Royal York Property Management is hiring a highly experienced Director of Operations to lead and strengthen the day-to-day operations of a growing, service-driven property management company.

This is a senior leadership role with responsibility across people, process, service quality, financial discipline, technology, compliance, vendor management, and execution.

The Director of Operations will oversee managers and operational departments, improve performance, enforce service standards, strengthen reporting, and build scalable systems across the business.

Royal York manages single-family residential rental homes, which means operations involve owners, tenants, maintenance issues, rent payments, complaints, legal timelines, vendors, communication standards, and service expectations. The right candidate must be able to lead in a fast-moving environment where accountability, documentation, customer experience, and operational discipline all matter.

This role has the potential to grow into a COO-level position for the right person.

How to Apply

Please submit your resume for consideration. Qualified candidates will receive an email within 24-48 hours of applying with a link to complete a pre-recorded online interview. This interview is required as part of the first stage of the hiring process.

After the pre-recorded interview is completed, our recruiting team will review your application and contact selected candidates by email regarding next steps.

Key Responsibilities

Lead managers, team leads, and operational departments
Improve operating processes, service standards, and team accountability
Ensure owners, tenants, vendors, and internal teams receive clear and timely communication
Enforce service standards across maintenance, leasing, collections, complaints, escalations, and customer communication
Strengthen rent collection, payment follow-up, receivables discipline, and financial accountability
Improve documentation, compliance, legal escalation, and risk-control processes
Build dashboards, scorecards, reporting systems, and management routines
Audit CRM and operational data to ensure reports reflect business reality
Identify root causes when performance drops and implement corrective action
Work with CRM systems, automation, AI tools, customer portals, dashboards, and third-party platforms
Translate operational problems into clear requirements for technical teams and software partners
Manage vendors, service providers, software vendors, and cross-company partnerships
Control costs while protecting service quality, compliance, collections, and customer experience
Coach, develop, restructure, or replace managers when required

Required Experience

10+ years of operations leadership experience
5+ years in a senior operations role managing managers, department heads, or multiple operational teams
Experience leading a high-volume, people-heavy service operation
Experience overseeing teams of 50+ people, either directly or through managers, team leads, contractors, vendors, or distributed operational staff
Strong experience with customer experience, service delivery, process improvement, team accountability, and operational performance
Experience with collections, payment follow-up, receivables, financial accountability, or payment-related operating controls
Strong judgment around documentation, compliance, escalation, risk control, and operational discipline
Experience with CRM systems, dashboards, workflow tools, reporting, automation, or AI-enabled systems
Experience managing vendors, partners, external service providers, software vendors, or cross-company relationships
Ability to work with technical teams and translate business needs into clear system, workflow, automation, or reporting requirements

Education Requirement

Bachelor’s degree required; Master’s degree preferred
Preferred fields of study include Business Administration, Operations Management, Management, Finance, Accounting, Economics, Real Estate, Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Information Systems, Technology Management, or a related field
MBA, Master’s in Management, Master’s in Operations, or similar graduate degree is considered an asset

Preferred Industry Background

Property management experience is valuable, but it is not the only relevant background. Strong candidates may come from industries such as:

Property management
Residential real estate operations
Leasing operations
Maintenance or field service operations
Telecom operations
Insurance claims or service operations
Automotive service operations
Financial services, collections, or receivables operations
Call centre or customer service operations
Logistics or dispatch operations
Hospitality or multi-location service businesses
Home services
Marketplace or platform-based operations
SaaS-enabled operations

Technology Expectations

Royal York is a tech-enabled property management company. The Director of Operations must be comfortable working with CRM systems, dashboards, automation, AI tools, customer portals, reporting platforms, and third-party technology partners.

This role does not require coding experience, but it does require the ability to work effectively with technical teams, explain operational problems clearly, and help improve systems that support the business.

What Success Looks Like

Within the first 90 days, success should include stronger visibility into operational performance, improved reporting and scorecards, clearer service standards, stronger manager accountability, better escalation rules, and a practical plan to improve customer experience, profitability, compliance, and scalability.

Long term, the goal is for this person to help Royal York become more disciplined, more scalable, more profitable, more technology-enabled, and more consistent across every part of the operation.

jobs.title: Chief Executive Officer
jobs.description:
About The Company

The Northwest Territories Power Corporation (NTPC)
is the primary public electricity utility serving the Northwest Territories and plays a critical role in supporting the territory's economic development, community well-being, and energy security. As a crown corporation wholly owned by the Government of the Northwest Territories through NT Hydro, NTPC is responsible for generating, transmitting, and distributing electricity across one of the most geographically vast and operationally challenging jurisdictions in North America. The organization provides power to more than 43,000 residents across 27 communities and manages a diverse portfolio of hydroelectric, diesel, natural gas, solar, wind, and battery storage assets. With more than $650 million in assets and approximately 151 MW of generating capacity, NTPC operates a geographically dispersed and operationally diverse utility system across the Northwest Territories.

For more information, please download the full position profile: NTPC CEO Position Profile.pdf

Position Overview

Reporting to the Board of Directors, the President and Chief Executive Officer (CEO) is responsible for providing the strategic, operational, financial, and cultural leadership required to guide the Northwest Territories Power Corporation (NTPC), Northwest Territories Hydro (NT Hydro), and their subsidiaries. The CEO will ensure the organizations effectively fulfill their commercial and public-service mandates while aligning with the strategic priorities of the Government of the Northwest Territories and the evolving needs of residents, communities, businesses, and industrial customers across the North.

The CEO will provide the leadership required to advance NTPC's mandate as the Northwest Territories' leading electricity utility while supporting the priorities of the Board of Directors and shareholder. Operating at the intersection of public policy, utility operations, infrastructure investment, and economic development, the CEO will guide the organization through a period of significant transformation as it addresses aging infrastructure, increasing energy demand, major capital investment requirements, and the transition toward a more sustainable and diversified energy future. This will require a strategic yet pragmatic leader who can establish a clear long-term direction while remaining accessible, hands-on when required, and closely connected to the operational realities of delivering critical utility services across the North.

Working within a highly regulated and publicly accountable environment, the CEO will balance the operational and commercial requirements of the Corporation with broader territorial priorities. This includes advancing strategic initiatives related to system reliability, affordability, renewable energy integration, Indigenous partnerships, economic development, and long-term energy security, while ensuring strong financial stewardship, operational excellence, and organizational performance. Preparing NTPC for future growth will be a central leadership mandate, requiring the CEO to ensure the Corporation has the people, leadership capacity, systems, infrastructure, partnerships, and financial readiness required to respond to increasing demand and emerging opportunities across the Northwest Territories.

The successful candidate will bring the judgment, political acumen, and stakeholder leadership required to navigate a complex operating environment and build trusted relationships with government, regulators, Indigenous governments, communities, customers, employees, and industry partners. Beyond delivering operational and financial results, the CEO will be expected to foster a culture of safety, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement while positioning NTPC for long-term operational, financial, and environmental sustainability and ensuring the reliable delivery of affordable energy to communities across the Northwest Territories.

Education And Experience Requirements

Education and Professional Background

Bachelor’s degree in engineering, commerce or other related discipline.
Significant senior leadership experience within the utility sector or a similarly complex, capital-intensive, highly regulated environment.
Experience leading organizations with significant operational, infrastructure, stakeholder, and public accountability requirements will be highly valued.
Minimum of eight years of direct management experience, in a unionized work environment.
Previous experience providing advice to and receiving direction from a Board of Directors.

WORK ARRANGEMENT

The role is based at NTPC’s head office in Hay River and requires a visible leadership presence within the organization and community. Regular travel to Yellowknife and NTPC’s regional plants, offices, and communities throughout the Northwest Territories is required. This may include travel by small aircraft and extended stays due to weather or operational requirements. The demands of the role may also require work outside normal office hours.

RECRUITMENT PROCESS

We welcome conversations with individuals interested in learning more about this unique leadership opportunity. To explore the role in confidence, please contact a member of our Executive Search team at MNP.

To apply, please submit a résumé and cover letter in confidence through MNP's online application portal or directly to the contacts below. All inquiries and applications will be managed through MNP to ensure a fair, confidential, and consistent recruitment process.

The Northwest Territories Power Corporation is committed to building a representative workforce and values the contributions of Indigenous peoples. Qualified Indigenous candidates are encouraged to self-identify during the application process and may be eligible for consideration under NTPC's Indigenous Employment Policy.

We thank all applicants for their interest; however, only those selected to move forward in the process will be contacted.

The work you'll do is more than just a job.

At the State of Minnesota, employees play a critical role in developing policies, providing essential services, and working to improve the well-being and quality of life for all Minnesotans. The State of Minnesota is committed to equity and inclusion, and invests in employees by providing benefits, support resources, and training and development opportunities.

The Department of Children, Youth, and Families administers programs, including affordable child care, child safety and permanency, food assistance, and more that are essential infrastructure for families, our workforce and the economic vitality of Minnesota. This position will direct and oversee financial operations, including payments, accounting, procurement, and financial reporting, for over $3.7 billion in annual expenditures supporting Minnesotans. It is the lead expert responsible for all accounting, financial reporting, and procurement functions. This includes specialized operations supporting DCYF’s state and federally financed programs. The position is responsible for integrating payment, accounting, and purchasing functions to ensure the agency operates with sound financial practices, internal controls, and meets fiduciary responsibilities.

Direct the development and implementation of financial and management reporting systems to ensure sound internal controls are maintained over agency resources and assure that all state and federal awards are managed in accordance with applicable laws and regulations
Direct all accounting functions for DCYF assets, expenditures, and revenue to ensure compliance with state and federal regulations, policies, and standards.
Represent the Chief Financial Officer and serve as a member of the senior finance leadership team for executive leadership, external leadership, and public audiences.
Direct the division’s personnel activity so that staff are utilized in an effective manner and that labor agreement contracts and plans are equitably administered.

Experience developing detailed financial operations for a large, complex organization including creation, implementation, and management of accounting, reporting, and payment processes at a business unit or division level.
Strong experience designing, implementing, and maintaining financial processes, including regular system updates and the development of technical and procedural controls that ensure alignment with business objectives and compliance with professional, legislative and operational standards.

This realigns state government to advance equitable outcomes for children, youth, and families through transformative, partnership-driven policies, programs and practices.

jobs.title: Chief Administrative Officer
jobs.description:
Oakville, Ontario, a community of more than 244,000 residents, stands out as a place where both people and business thrive. Located in the west end of the Greater Toronto Area, the town blends economic strength with an exceptional quality of life, making it one of Canada’s most desirable places in which to live and invest. It consistently ranks among the country’s most livable communities and has been recognized for seven consecutive years as one of Site Selection magazine’s top 20 Canadian locations for investment.

Oakville offers ready access to domestic and global markets, strengthened by its proximity to leading post‐secondary institutions that provide talent, research capacity, and industry partnerships. Located only 30 minutes from downtown Toronto, Oakville combines exceptional connectivity with strong academic links that support innovation and business growth.

Oakville offers a lifestyle that ranks among the best in Canada, with established neighborhoods, acclaimed schools, abundant parklands, and a strong sense of community. Quality of life is a defining feature, attracting business leaders, entrepreneurs, and employees who value a place where both work and life can thrive. This blend of natural beauty, vibrant amenities, and supportive community spirit makes Oakville a destination of choice for living, working, and growing.

With a 2026 operating budget of $458 million, a capital budget of over $344 million and over 1,700 permanent and part-time staff, the Town of Oakville is committed to meeting the needs of our residents and business community by delivering efficient and effective services that reflect their community values.

Inspire our Future as our Chief Administrative Officer

The ideal candidate will be an experienced, trusted and collaborative leader with a proven track record of results and accomplishments in municipal government. You have exceptional communication skills and the political acumen to interact with diverse interest holders to foster the development of partnerships, engage and inspire our employees, while ensuring customer service excellence.

Reporting to the Mayor and Council, the Chief Administrative Officer
is responsible for the strategic leadership and efficient delivery of all the municipality’s administrative and operational services. As the key advisor to Mayor and Council, you will work closely with elected officials to develop and implement operational plans and ensure the coordination of services which align to and support our strategic priorities. You will recommend policies, plans, and programs that benefit our residents by being efficient, accountable and fiscally sound. You will work to enhance growth and development in the community as well as ensure the effective utilization of resources through the priorities and guiding principles in our strategic plan.

Leading a talented team of staff and working in a complex unionized environment, this position guides and inspires a dedicated workforce and helps foster a workplace culture focused on service excellence, innovative thinking, and teamwork while positioning the Town of Oakville as an employer of choice.

The Town offers a competitive total rewards package including benefits, vacation and pension. The Town strives to promote and demonstrate the values of Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion. We are committed to reflecting the diversity of the community we serve and encourage qualified candidates of all backgrounds and abilities to self-identify in their application. jobs.title: Director of Legal Operations
jobs.description:
A Note On How To Reach Us

We're truly grateful that so many people have Foundant on their radar — it means a lot that our work resonates with others. That said, due to the high volume of direct messages and emails we receive, cold outreach isn't the preferred way to be considered for a role, and we're not able to prioritize applications submitted this way. To apply for open positions, please visit our careers page, which is the fastest and most effective route to being considered.

About Foundant

At Foundant, we build mission-critical software for the social good ecosystem — helping foundations, grantmakers, nonprofits, and community organizations streamline their work, strengthen relationships, and maximize their impact. We serve the giving community worldwide with a comprehensive suite of solutions spanning grant management, community foundation software, and giving analytics.

We're a unified company shaped by strong roots across our product portfolio, and we operate with intention and purpose. Our team of ~350 people across six countries is connected by a shared North Star: to be the trusted partner and strategic advisor to the communities we serve.

Where You’ll Work

As a remote-first workplace, we believe in offering flexibility and the freedom to work where it suits you best, while staying connected through technology. Our global network of talent is supported by physical office hubs and virtual collaboration, fostering a dynamic environment where innovation and growth thrive.
With office locations in Bozeman, MT, Toronto, Canada, and Dublin, Ireland, you'll be part of a globally connected team. Whether you're working remotely or from one of our office locations, you'll be contributing to a vibrant, collaborative culture focused on driving meaningful impact across the world.

What You’ll Do

You’ll own execution of sales contracts through our CLM system, administering attorney-approved playbooks and partnering with Sales and Deal Desk to keep contracts moving efficiently through the pipeline
You’ll escalate terms that require legal review to the appropriate attorney, with clear context so review stays fast and targeted
You’ll own the legal department’s operational infrastructure — budget, technology stack (CLM, e-billing, matter management), and vendor relationships
You’ll manage outside counsel relationships and spend
You’ll design and maintain legal team metrics and reporting — matter volume, cycle time, response time SLAs, playbook usage, and spend against budget — for the General Counsel
You’ll drive continuous improvement across the legal function, refining our CLM to get more value from the tool we already have, and keeping playbooks and workflows current
You’ll partner with Finance, GRC, Sales Operations, and IS on systems, budgeting, and tooling decisions
You’ll support departmental planning, including headcount, budget forecasting, and resource allocation
Other duties as assigned

What You’ll Need

Bachelor’s degree required, plus one additional graduate-level degree (J.D. strongly preferred)
5+ years of experience in legal operations
3+ years working within a SaaS or PaaS legal department, focused on contract negotiation and management using legal-approved playbooks
Strong proficiency in Microsoft 365 and Salesforce
Strong understanding of effective AI use cases in legal operations
Prior experience with Ironclad a plus
Must be legally eligible to work in the United States

What You’ll Bring To Our Team Dynamics

Leadership Competencies

Strategic Thinking — Owns the legal department’s technology stack, budget, and vendor relationships, translating tooling and process decisions into measurable improvements in how the legal team operates
Decision-Making — Determines when a contract term needs attorney review and routes it with enough context for a fast, well-informed decision
Performance Advancement — Moves contracts through the CLM with urgency, without sacrificing the accuracy of playbook application, metrics, and reporting the GC relies on
Collaboration and Learning — Sets clear expectations with Sales, Deal Desk, and other partner departments, acting as a facilitator who keeps deals moving rather than a bottleneck for legal review
Change Management — Leads adoption of CLM and playbook updates across Sales and Deal Desk, making sure changes actually stick in day-to-day use

Why You’ll Love Working At Foundant

At the heart of everything we do is a commitment to innovation and making a positive impact. Whether you’re working on projects that empower not-for-profits, community foundations, or corporations, your contributions will help drive real-world change.
We offer competitive salary and benefits, including tuition, and lifestyle reimbursements, and bespoke mindfulness and fitness initiatives.
With our Flexible PTO policy, you’ll have the freedom to manage your time in a way that supports your personal well-being and professional success.
We’re committed to your professional and personal development. With our merger, you'll have the chance to collaborate across teams, giving you exposure to diverse ideas, expertise, and projects that span multiple industries.
As part of a larger organization, you’ll have even more opportunities to grow your career. Whether it’s exploring new roles, leadership opportunities, or shifting to a different department, we support internal mobility to help you achieve your career goals
You’ll enjoy autonomy and responsibility, empowering you to approach your work creatively and independently, fostering innovation and independent thought.
Employee recognition is a core part of our culture. When you do a great job, we make sure everyone knows about it!

Foundant is an equal opportunity employer, committed to building a diverse workforce that represents the communities we serve. We welcome and encourage applications from all qualified candidates, and will consider all applicants without regard to race, color, citizenship, religion, sex, marital/family status, sexual orientation, gender identity, Indigenous status, age, disability, or individuals who may require accommodation.

Foundant is also committed to providing accommodations throughout the interview and employment process. Accommodations are available upon request for candidates participating in all aspects of the selection process. If you have accessibility requirements during the recruitment process and require accommodation, please contact hr@smartsimple.com.

new_jobs.description:
Job Description

What is the opportunity?

As Director, Financial Crimes Risk Assessment you are responsible for the design and execution of the enterprise risk assessment. In this role, you will identify and assess inherent risks and control effectiveness, demonstrate compliance, and identify opportunities to optimize the financial crimes program, by:

Leading the enterprise-wide assessment of financial crimes risks and controls globally and across RBC Platforms, businesses units, and jurisdictions.
Leading the development of capabilities to enable the quantitative and qualitative assessment of inherent risks, control effectiveness, and residual risk.
Performing expert analysis to identify concentrations of risk and adequacy of controls to ultimately inform and recommend risk mitigation strategies.
Delivering high-quality risk assessment products to support regulatory compliance and inform business decisions.
Remaining abreast of emerging risks and evolving regulatory environment to continuously refine RBC’s risk assessment approach.

What will you do?

Lead the efficient and effective execution of enterprise-wide risk assessment activities, in line with regulatory and business expectations.
Lead the development and continuous improvement of the Enterprise Risk Assessment Methodology and operating procedures.
Identify gaps and opportunities to enhance risk assessment data integration, tools, and processes to drive efficiency and consistency across assessments.
Identify requirements for analytic tools and capabilities to perform quantitative and qualitative assessments of inherent risks, controls and residual risk
Collaborate across financial crimes program to establish risk rating frameworks, validate results, align on mitigation strategies and produce reports.
Establish roadmaps and provide regular reporting on risk assessment activities including data collection and integration, analysis and report generation.
Identify and escalate material risk exposures and control gaps
Support regulatory exams, audits and internal reviews related to risk assessment activities
Monitor changes in AML/ATF regulations and participate in industry related initiatives to remain abreast of existing and new laws and regulatory expectations

What do you need to succeed?

Must have

Post-secondary education or equivalent
Proven experience with executing financial crime risk assessments
Strong ability to evaluate and design risk assessment capabilities and tools
Deep understanding of global financial crime regulatory environment
Ability to synthesize complex data into clear, actionable insights
Experience working with cross-functional teams
Project management

Nice to have

Graduate degree (MBA or relevant subject matter area)
Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist (CAMS) designation or other related certifications

What’s in it for you?

We thrive on the challenge to be our best, progressive thinking to keep growing, and working together to deliver trusted advice to help our clients thrive and communities prosper. We care about each other, reaching our potential, making a difference to our communities, and achieving success that is mutual.

A comprehensive Total Rewards Program including bonuses and flexible benefits, competitive compensation, commissions, and stock where applicable
Leaders who support your development through coaching and managing opportunities
Work in a dynamic, collaborative, progressive, and high-performing team
To be part of a large and growing global organization which puts client interests first and has a culture of fairness and accountability

Job Skills

Anti-Money Laundering (AML), Control Analysis, Cross-Functional Leadership, Data Analysis, Data Literacy, Executive Reports, Financial Crimes Compliance, People Management, Professional Writing, Project Management, Regulatory Risk, Risk Assessments, Risk Mitigation Strategies
